precepts.text: Seek the kingdom of heaven first, and everything else shall be added unto thee. That's what the Bible says.
precepts.point: Sometimes your job, whatever you have, becomes more important, and then you wonder why you can't grow. Our chief love is the word of God. Jobs or careers is just for us to get by in this captivity. It should not be a focal point in your life. Matthew 6:33, I believe it is. Seek the kingdom of heaven first, and everything else shall be added unto thee. That's what the Bible says. So look what it says. What verse was that? Verse eight. Verse nine.

note.label: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

precepts.why:
Solomon says “I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.” Sometimes your job, whatever you have, becomes more important, and then you wonder why you can’t grow. Our chief love is the word of God. Jobs and careers are just for us to get by in this captivity; they should not be the focal point of your life. That is Matthew 6:33: seek the kingdom first, and everything else shall be added unto thee. That’s what the Bible says.

“Wherefore I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon God, and the spirit of wisdom came to me.” That does not mean you just pray, God, give me understanding so I can break down Revelation. You pray to God, and God will tell you to study to show thyself approved and rightly divide the word. You have to choose this, and make him first.

“All gold in respect of her is as a little sand, and silver shall be counted as clay before her.” Why is wisdom better than gold and silver? Those things are corruptible: they can be stolen or destroyed, and when you sell them the money runs out quick. Wisdom never runs out, because with wisdom you get the understanding to make more and to do this and that.

“I loved her above health and beauty, and chose to have her instead of light: for the light that cometh from her never goeth out.” I choose wisdom above all things; I prefer the Lord above all things. If you want understanding, call upon God and he will give it, but we have to make him first. Wisdom is “a treasure unto men that never faileth: which they that use become the friends of God”, and seeking that first is the beginning of the transition from milk to meat.

precepts.text: When they therefore were come together, they asked of him, saying, Lord. The apostles, the disciples, when they were come together, they asked of Jesus Christ, saying what? Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel? Restore the kingdom to Israel. So Christ's kingdom is Israel's kingdom as well. You all understand that? So we are asking for Christ to bring us the kingdom, because we are joint heirs with him.
precepts.point: Thy kingdom come. So Christ said pray to the Lord for his kingdom to be done on earth. We are joint heirs with him. So what are we actually praying for? We are praying for our kingdom as well.

note.label: The Exponential Maturation In The Days Of Decadence

precepts.why:
“Thy kingdom come.” Christ said to pray for the Lord's kingdom to come on earth. We are joint heirs with him, so what are we actually praying for? Our kingdom as well.

“When they therefore were come together, they asked of him, saying, Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?” The apostles, when they came together, asked Christ to restore the kingdom to Israel. So Christ's kingdom is Israel's kingdom as well. We are asking Christ to bring us the kingdom, because we are joint heirs with him.

We have always wanted to know when it is coming. Ezra asked it: “What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first, and the beginning of it that followeth?” When shall be the end of the first world we are subjugated to, in bondage under, and the beginning of our kingdom, where the saints can rejoice in glory? The disciples asked it on the mount of Olives: “Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world?” Christ told them to learn the parable of the fig tree: when the branch is tender and puts forth leaves, you know summer is nigh. “So likewise ye, when ye shall see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors.” When you see the decadence of this society, know that the tribulation and the destruction are near, even at the doors.

And God told Ezra what to watch: “For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.” Jacob's hand held fast Esau's heel for a reason. When Esau goes down, we come up; when Esau is destroyed, we are in our kingdom. That's why the churches don't teach about Esau: the people at the top know, and they make sure it's hidden. So every time you pray thy kingdom come, you are praying for the destruction of the present kingdom. Christ's kingdom is not going to rule beside Babylon the Great; Christ isn't setting a throne beside the president.

precepts.text: Thy will be done in earth. And the Lord's will will be done in earth, because this is the will that we want. I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart. The laws of God are within our hearts. So we want what God wants. That is why he says be ye perfect. He is telling us to be perfect, even as our Father is perfect. So the objective is for us to become one with him. Our objective is to become one with Christ, one with the Most High, one with the angels. That is the hierarchy that the Most High is setting up. We are his heirs. We are his ambassadors on this earth. And that is why he gave us the name Israel. We are the prince of him. We are the prince of his power. That is us. That is not anybody else. That is us.
precepts.point: Thy kingdom come. So Christ said pray to the Lord for his kingdom to be done on earth. We are joint heirs with him. So what are we actually praying for? We are praying for our kingdom as well.

note.label: The Exponential Maturation In The Days Of Decadence

precepts.why:
“Thy will be done in earth.” The Lord's will will be done in earth, because this is the will that we want. David said it: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” The laws of God are within our hearts, so we want what God wants. That's why he says be ye perfect, even as our Father is perfect. The objective is to become one with him: one with Christ, one with the Most High, one with the angels. That's the hierarchy the Most High is setting up. We are his heirs, his ambassadors on this earth, and that's why he gave us the name Israel. We are the prince of his power. That's us, not anybody else.

If the will of God is going to be done in this earth, and there is a will here already, then this will has got to be destroyed. Two kings cannot sit on the same throne. “The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof.” Notice: is given. Esau took the planet and ruled it in evil, yes, but God gave him the power to do so, for a time, and when that time is up it's over.

“What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction.” Esau struts with his chest out, bombing countries and stealing their resources, their minds, their women, and everybody wants to look like him. And the Most High says, I'm the one who put him up there, so that I can destroy him and everybody will know I'm the true power. The Lord endures with longsuffering because he will not break his word: he gave this man a time to rule, until the times of the nations be fulfilled. The whole nation of Edom is the vessels of wrath, a channel through which God shows how angry and how powerful he is, fitted to destruction, created for that purpose, just as he set up Pharaoh.

These are diabolical, demonic people; look at James Byrd dragged through the streets of Jasper, Texas. That's not teaching hatred; it's the facts. There's no such thing as a nice snake. Stick by these commandments. Come out from among them, be separate, gather yourselves together, organize and prepare for your kingdom while he brings this kingdom down. That is the maturing we have to do.

precepts.text: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also. Wherever your treasure is, that is where your mind is going to be occupied. If your mind is filled with games and sports statistics, that is where you are building your treasures, and all of that is going to be destroyed. Occupy your mind in the laws of God: how to unify, how can I be used as a tool for the Lord's army, how can I be utilized to push this truth further. That is laying up treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt.
precepts.point: Wherefore I give you to understand, that no man speaking by the Spirit of God calleth Jesus accursed: and that no man can say that Jesus is the Lord, but by the Holy Ghost. By him actions are weighed. Somebody speaking of Christ and calling him accursed, that is not of the Lord; somebody who confessed Christ is Lord, this person believes.

note.label: Members of the Body  Pt2

precepts.why:
Following what the Deacon brought out, Christ says: “For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.” Wherever your treasure is, that is where your mind is going to be occupied.

If your mind is filled with Mortal Kombat moves and the stats of the greatest to ever play any sport, that is where your focus is and that is where you are building up your treasures. “Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal”. All of those carnal things are going to be destroyed, so that should not be where your focus is.

“But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt”. When you occupy your mind in the laws of God, that is where you are laying up your treasure: how to unify, how can I be used as a tool for the Lord's army, how can I be utilized to push this truth further. That is where our minds should be: on treasure that cannot be corrupted, that no rust or moth can touch.

precepts.text: If thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light. A leader is locked in with laser focus, and everybody under him becomes the same.
precepts.point: Any task set before our forefathers got done: the Maccabees who were not warriors, the slaves who left Egypt. Egypt was America. If the shooting starts, we know scripturally what happens; the Lord takes care of it.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
The people built the wall because they “had a mind to work.” This is how a leader’s mindset must be, and Christ shows it: “The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.”

A single eye is being locked in, what they call laser focus. Whatever you are locked in on, that is what you are going to see. That is all you are going to see, and that is all that matters.

And when the leader is like that, guess who else is going to be like that? Everybody underneath him. The single eye of the one at the head fills the whole body with light, so the whole camp takes on his focus.

That is why the wall got built. The mind to work in the people starts with the mind of the one leading them.

precepts.text: When thou doest alms, sound not a trumpet as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and streets; when thou prayest, be not as the hypocrites who love to pray standing in the corners of the streets to be seen of men. They have their reward.
precepts.point: The hypocrites of our people: Isaiah 9:16-17, the leaders of this people cause them to err, the religious and political leaders, T.D. Jakes and Pastor P, and they that are led of them are destroyed; the Lord has no joy in their young men nor mercy on their fatherless and widows, for every one is an hypocrite and evil doer and every mouth speaketh folly. They all have the Bible and say they believe in Jesus and do not one word of it.

note.label: Hope Amid Destruction

precepts.why:
When the Bible calls our people hypocrites, look at the hypocrisy. “Therefore when thou doest thine alms, do not sound a trumpet before thee, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may have glory of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.” Christ was condemning the Pharisees, who gave their alms publicly and made a big announcement that they gave such an amount of money so everybody could see.

“But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth: That thine alms may be in secret: and thy Father which seeth in secret himself shall reward thee openly.”

Now look at Marvin Winans at Perfecting Church. A grandmother stands up to sow her seed of a thousand plus two hundred thirty-five dollars before everybody, and he embarrasses her: y'all not listening, I said a thousand plus a thousand. She says she'll work on the other eight hundred, and he says that ain't what I asked you to do, and the organ goes right on playing like it agreed. That is what the Pharisees were doing, sounding a trumpet in the synagogue.

“And when thou prayest, thou shalt not be as the hypocrites are: for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.” And there are thousands praying in the streets in California to be seen: that is what Christ said not to do. Those are all Christians.

The Pharisees were our people, and the hypocrites of Isaiah 33 whom fearfulness will surprise are our people in these churches today, doing the very things Christ condemned.

precepts.text: O death, how bitter is the remembrance of thee to a man that liveth at rest in his possessions. The fear of death is often the fear of leaving things behind. In this truth you cannot get attached to things; the saints love not their lives unto death.
precepts.point: No man can serve two masters; ye cannot serve God and mammon. Mammon is money. The elite want nothing to do with God because they think they are in their heaven already.

note.label: Covetous Eyes Will Be Put Out

precepts.why:
“Ye cannot serve God and mammon.” Mammon is money. That is why the elite do not want to hear anything about God: they feel like they are in their heaven already. And that is why a lot of people are scared of dying. Many times the fear of death is not death itself.

“O death, how bitter is the remembrance of thee to a man that liveth at rest in his possessions”. That man is living so good that the moment he thinks of death, he says, I have to leave all this behind? Because of his possessions his mind is on here. He is not thinking about the possession over there, what the Most High has in store for us that eyes have not seen and ears have not heard. He wants it now.

“Unto the man that hath nothing to vex him, and that hath prosperity in all things: yea, unto him that is yet able to receive meat!” Do you think a covetous man wants to die, after he just got that nice Porsche and bought that nice house? No. He needs to enjoy it a little more, because it is never enough to a covetous man.

That is why in this truth you cannot get attached to things. The saints love not their lives unto death. Nothing on this planet can hold us back from doing what we are supposed to be doing, and whatever is going to happen to us is what will happen; the apostles were appointed last, unto death. You cannot hold to money and serve God too.

precepts.text: Thy kingdom come, thy will be done in earth as it is in heaven.
precepts.point: Those who believe enter into rest, and those who did not believe were kept out.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.” We want God's kingdom to be in earth as it is in heaven, and that is what we are praying for right now: the kingdom of heaven on the earth.

This ties to the rest of Hebrews 4. When Genesis says God “rested on the seventh day from all his work”, it does not mean God was tired and went to get some sleep. Moses is an analogy, a similitude. Hebrews says “he spake in a certain place of the seventh day”: God's rest is a place, paradise. 2 Esdras 3:6 says God led Adam “into paradise, which thy right hand had planted, before ever the earth came forward.” Paradise was planted before the earth, and leading Adam into paradise is entering into his rest.

That is the kingdom of Adam. When Adam had dominion on the earth, it was on a much higher level than people think. Adam had access to the spirit realm and could go back and forth, the only flesh, him and his wife, that could, until he committed sin; flesh and blood cannot be up there because of that sinful nature. How Adam was on the earth is basically how we are going to be in the future, the difference being that he was not in the flesh as we are. So when we pray “Thy kingdom come”, we are praying for what was once on the earth in Adam's day to be on the earth again.

precepts.text: No man can serve two masters; ye cannot serve God and mammon.
precepts.point: Friendship with the world is enmity with God, and makes you an adulterer against him.

note.label: Kill Or Be Killed

precepts.why:
On the line of adultery and lust and the love of the world, Christ said: “No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.”

A decision has to be made. Either you hate God, have enmity against him, and love the other, or you hold to the one and despise the other. The other can be money, your career, your bed because you don’t want to be here, a Christmas stocking full of abominations. Some snuck off and celebrated the devastation of their brothers, the slaughter of the tribe of Gad, got a turkey drumstick, watched the football game, then came back saying shalom, Most High in Christ bless. Many will hold on to the world and despise the heavenly Father.

You cannot serve the God of the nation of Israel and mammon. Brothers and sisters are more loyal to their jobs and the white man who runs the corporations, who can terminate your contract after fifteen years of loyalty just as you are getting ready to retire. That is serving mammon.

James calls it what it is: “Ye adulterers and adulteresses.” When these other things have become a god, you have committed adultery against the heavenly Father. Many do not hate the world; they hate having to change and repent. That is the war in your members, and you have to kill that adulterous spirit inside you or it will kill you.

precepts.text: Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt. So the treasures on earth — crypto coins, Bitcoin, the computers could blow up, money is going to burn, gold could melt — and where thieves break through and steal. Somebody could steal it. But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven. But the treasure we should lay up is what? The treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt. Because the treasure in heaven, that eternal life we are all striving for, nothing can take that away from us once we achieve it. And where thieves do not break through nor steal. No thieves can break through and get those things, what the Lord has prepared for us in paradise. No thief can take that away from us once we attain it. But we have got to get there.
precepts.point: Now, we are not talking about gold or diamonds or crypto or NFTs. Let us see what type of treasure the Bible is talking about that you lay up for yourself when you honour your father and respect your mother.

note.label: Honor Thy Father & Thy Mother

precepts.why:
Sirach says “he that honoureth his mother is as one that layeth up treasure.” We are not talking about gold or diamonds or crypto or NFTs. Christ shows what kind of treasure it is.

“Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal”. The treasures on earth, crypto coins and Bitcoin, can go when the computers blow up; money is going to burn; gold can melt; somebody can steal it.

“But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal”. The treasure in heaven is the eternal life we are all striving for. Nothing can take that away from us once we attain it, and no thief can break through and get what the Lord has prepared for us in paradise.

So honouring and respecting your mother is laying up that treasure in heaven. But we have got to get there.

precepts.text: Seek ye first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things shall be added; the Lord sees the sacrifice it takes to get to the congregation.
precepts.point: For the brothers and sisters far from a congregation: you may have to travel and you may have to be the firstfruits in your area. The first assemblies met in houses, and that is how camps start; a man will drive hours to a club, so drive for the truth, and the Lord honors that faith.

note.label: Exodus 16: Manna From Heaven and the Sabbath Proved

precepts.why:
Getting to the congregation on the sabbath takes sacrifice, especially for those far from one. “But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.” Seek the kingdom first; the rest is added.

A man will drive hours to a club, so drive for the truth. The Lord sees the sacrifice it takes to get to the congregation and honors that faith. The sabbath is the holy convocation, and he who seeks first the kingdom to keep it is the one all these things are added to.

precepts.text: Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven; the tabernacle on earth answered to the heavenly.
precepts.point: What was built in the wilderness was a shadow of what is in the heavens. The Most High is the architect, and He showed Moses the pattern of a heavenly tabernacle to be made for Israel on earth; thy kingdom come, thy will be done in earth as it is in heaven, is an example of that same order.

note.label: Exodus 26: The Pattern Shown in the Mount

precepts.why:
“Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.”

That is the same order as the tabernacle. What is in heaven was shown to Moses in the mount and made on earth for Israel, according to the pattern. The prayer that God’s will be done in earth as it is in heaven is an example of that same order: the heavenly brought down to the earth.

precepts.text: The bountiful reaping may be treasures laid up in heaven rather than riches in this life.
precepts.point: He which soweth sparingly shall reap sparingly, and he which soweth bountifully shall reap bountifully; that does not mean the Most High blesses you with a three story house, for you may be storing up treasures in heaven. Give as you purpose in your heart, not grudgingly or of necessity, for God loveth a cheerful giver; giving with an attitude is worse than keeping the money.

note.label: Exodus 38: The Altar, the Court, and the Sum of the Offering

precepts.why:
“But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal”.

He which soweth bountifully shall reap bountifully, but the reaping is not necessarily a three story house in this life. The bountiful reaping may be treasures laid up in heaven rather than riches here. That is what the thousands of men gave toward with their half shekels for the sanctuary, and what a cheerful giver gives toward today.

precepts.text: The light of the body is the eye; if thine eye be single thy whole body is full of light, but if thine eye be evil thy body is full of darkness; keep the commandment as the apple of your eye.
precepts.point: The statutes of the Lord are right, rejoicing the heart; the commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes. When the commandments enlighten your eyes you know where to walk, you will not stumble, you stay focused on keeping God's laws.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“the commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes.” Christ says, “The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light. But if thine eye be evil, thy whole body shall be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in thee be darkness, how great is that darkness!”

If your eye is single, your whole body is full of light; if it is evil, your body is full of darkness. Keep the commandment as the apple of your eye. When the commandments enlighten your eyes, you know where to walk, you will not stumble, and you stay focused on keeping God's laws.

precepts.text: Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil; for thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.
precepts.point: For he hath delivered me out of all trouble, and mine eye hath seen his desire upon mine enemies. We know the plans the Most High has to destroy them.

note.label: Psalm 54: Save Me by Thy Name

precepts.why: “For he hath delivered me out of all trouble: and mine eye hath seen his desire upon mine enemies.” Christ taught us to pray for the same: “lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.” Deliver us from evil is David's deliverance out of all trouble. And we know the plans the Most High has to destroy our enemies; the kingdom, the power and the glory are his for ever.

precepts.text: Lay not up treasures on earth where moth and rust corrupt, but treasures in heaven that cannot be corrupted or stolen.
precepts.point: Durable riches are not money, since lottery winners, entertainers and athletes end up broke. Durable riches are the treasures laid up in heaven, charity and helping your brother and sister in need.

note.label: Proverbs 8: Wisdom Crieth in the Streets and Christ Set Up from Everlasting

precepts.why:
“Riches and honour are with me; yea, durable riches and righteousness. My fruit is better than gold, yea, than fine gold; and my revenue than choice silver.” Durable riches are not money, since lottery winners, entertainers and athletes end up broke. Money is not durable.

Christ says where the durable riches are: “Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal”. Treasures on earth get corrupted and stolen; treasures in heaven cannot be.

Durable riches are the treasures laid up in heaven, charity and helping your brother and sister in need. That is the fruit of wisdom better than fine gold, and the substance she causes those that love her to inherit.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Breakdown Of Revelation 16

precepts.why: Christ gave us a secret, for those who have ears: “Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.” Many times we read it and don’t understand what it is saying. Read through Paul’s letters, there is a deeper understanding: what is going to be established on earth is a complete replica of exactly what is going on in the heavens. It is a prayer, but looked at spiritually there is more in that thing.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Breakdown Of Revelation 16

precepts.why: “And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil”: the evil of the temptation of sex or money. Satan can’t tempt you unless something is already in you: you cannot be tempted with a cigarette that was never your thing. Temptation, we are already told, is coming; lead us not into it means, Lord, don’t let us give in to the temptation, and deliver us from that evil.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 21 Thy Kingdom Come

precepts.why: “As the days of heaven upon the earth”: that’s what I want. Can we write these preachers a letter and let the congregants know: you are not growing wings, flying up to the by and by, playing harps on clouds, eating catfish and smoking cigars. That’s not happening. Everything will be on earth.
